Wang Lung (to the eldest son, the second son): "Well, and tomorrow I will go to my father's house and I will tell him that he must take his sons away from me and they must serve him on his land lest I forget the land and we die as the rich men die. I do not want a son of mine in my house who forgets the land."
the second son (to the eldest son, Wang Lung): "It is only the land that I have thought about,"
[action] (to the eldest son, the second son) leads sons to land

Wang Lung (to the eldest son, the second son): "Now, all this land that I have bought, it is mine and it is yours also, and it is mine and it is yours, and it is not mine to spend and it is not yours to spend, and we are earth, and we must eat the grain from it and we must plough it, lest we forget it and die as others die."
[action] points to well-cultivated fields

Wang Lung (to the eldest son, the second son): "Tomorrow we will all go to the west field and we will plow it, and you will each plow your half, and you will each pull the ox, for you are my sons and we are earth and we are fed by the land and we will not forget it."
[action] The second son begins to plow with the ox.
[action] (to the eldest son, the second son) tells sons to plow side by side
Wang Lung (to the eldest son, the second son): "Now we will plow side by side, as land and sons of the land, and you shall not plow separately like strangers, lest you forget us and forget the land."
[action] (to the eldest son) The second son carefully breaks the furrow, using the land as a model.

Wang Lung (to the eldest son, the second son): "I will plow the first furrow and you two shall follow me and each of you shall plow a furrow, and when we come to the middle we shall meet, and if you fall behind or if you stop you are dead men!"
[action] (to the second son) The eldest son breaks the furrow with his father, plowing hard.
[action] Wang Lung plows the land with his sons.
